limits_note: Fails on quota outright (0 GB). Also costs a state fee and requires an in-person card pickup at an embassy. So it is slower and pricier than any qualifying provider while delivering no bytes.
reliability_note: genuinely open to non-residents (that is its purpose) and would solve the identity problem for EU services generally, but carries no storage — recorded here because it is the canonical 'does e-residency come with storage' question and the answer is no.

evidence.proved: the four steps are: apply online, wait for approval and card delivery, pick up card in person ('bring with you your ID'), set up card with DigiDoc. No storage, hosting or cloud component anywhere in the process.
